# Policy Enforcement Summary (Phase C.2 Part B)

Generated 2026-08-01. All 46 `docs/policies/` files classified against `ast_call_graph.json` (2,218 nodes) + direct source reads. Full records: `policy_enforcement_raw.json`.

## Status counts (46/46 covered)

| ENFORCED | PARTIAL | CONTRADICTED | DOCUMENTED-ONLY | STALE-TOPOLOGY | DEAD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18 | 11 | 8 | 8 | 1 | 0 |

**Zero DEAD is deliberate.** CHA seeds every module's own `__main__` block as an entry point, so a
module can show `reachable_cha: true` purely from being a standalone CLI script, independent of
production use (confirmed for `anti_hallucination_enforcement.py`). Given that confound, ambiguous
cases were classified CONTRADICTED (positive evidence of a mismatch) or PARTIAL, reserving DEAD for a
confidently-unreachable case that did not arise here.

## STALE-TOPOLOGY: true count vs. the 16-file floor

Every eligible policy was retranslated to `Level 0/1/2` + `Steps 0-8` before classification.
Retranslation resolved 16 of the token-grep floor into other statuses via `LEGACY_MARKER_ALIASES`
(old Step 12/13/14 -> SDLC_STEP_6/7/8, ENFORCED there). Only **1 of 46** stayed STALE-TOPOLOGY after
retranslation (`intelligent-model-selection-policy.md`) -- one of its 5 inputs (plan-mode decision)
was itself deleted in v1.13, so the retranslated question is still unanswerable. Its sibling
`intelligent-decision-engine-policy.md` retranslates to "no current step of this kind exists" and was
classified CONTRADICTED instead -- the mechanism was removed, not renamed.

## Hook-coupling: description vs. implementation delta

- **4/4 match**: every policy naming a hook in its own text (`hook-system`,
  `implementation-execution`, `metrics-monitoring`, `tool-optimization`) is confirmed hook-coupled.
  No description-overclaims-hook cases found.
- **11 policies are hook-coupled without saying so**: `automatic-task-breakdown`,
  `common-failures-prevention`, `context-management`, `context-reading`, `git-auto-commit`,
  `session-memory`, `session-pruning`, `task-phase-enforcement`, `task-progress-tracking`,
  `tool-usage-optimization`, `version-release`. Three (`git-auto-commit`, `session-memory`,
  `session-pruning`) are hook-*coupled* but the coupled path silently no-ops (contradiction #2) --
  coupling to a hook != the hook's target actually running.

## Top contradictions (full detail in `contradictions.md`)

1. `callgraph-analysis-policy.md` (seeded) -- `MAX_FILES=300` makes impact-analysis blind to the
   entire `sdlc_pipeline/` package it's meant to analyze.
2. `session-memory` / `session-pruning` / `git-auto-commit` -- one root cause: the Stop hook (fires
   every turn) guards maintenance subprocesses with `.exists()` checks against
   `scripts/architecture/01-sync-system/` and `.../09-git-commit/`, neither of which exists on disk.
3. `architecture-script-mapping-policy.md` -- a document whose sole purpose is mapping
   `scripts/architecture/`'s contents is internally self-contradictory (3 vs. 6 in its own text) and
   names 12+ migration-target files that don't exist anywhere in the repo.
4. `anti-hallucination-enforcement.md` -- real code, zero production importers repo-wide.
5. `intelligent-decision-engine-policy.md` -- "OpenRouter consolidation" CLAUDE.md's own version
   history shows was never built; the 4 systems it claims to unify were deleted in v1.13.
6. `tool-usage-optimization-policy.md` -- self-claims "NO DUPLICATION" while sharing its one real
   enforcement point with `tool-optimization-policy.md` and a third overlapping standards file.

## Top 5 uncertainty notes

1. **CHA under-reports hook-policy liveness.** `pre-tool-enforcer.py` loads `core.py` via
   `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, which then aliases `policies/*.py` functions through
   module attributes rather than direct calls; the static pass can't trace either hop, so those
   functions show `reachable_cha: false` despite being confirmed live in `core.py`'s
   `_BLOCKING_POLICIES` list. This agent's own dispatch (gated by `agent_persona.py`) is first-hand
   proof the chain executes.
2. **Two policies' creation-side methods** (`documentation-update-policy.md`,
   `github-issues-integration-policy.md`) show `reachable_cha: false` on a class instantiated once in
   a wrapper file while sibling methods on the same class show `true` -- scored PARTIAL rather than
   DEAD given the same blind spot as note 1, not independently re-verified by call-site tracing.
3. **LHS's DDI/LCOM3/CBO inputs are a 20-module reduced sample**, drawn from the *highest-complexity*
   modules specifically -- see `lhs.json`'s `overall_caveat` for the resulting pessimism-bias risk.
4. **TestCoverage was entirely unavailable** for DDI; no coverage report exists in scope. `lhs.json`
   substitutes a DocCoverage-only proxy, explicitly flagged, not a fabricated figure.
5. **`task-progress-tracking-policy.md`** was scored PARTIAL/LOW-confidence on module-level evidence
   only, without tracing `task_tracking.py`'s check fn into `core.py`'s dispatch table like the 12
   PreToolUse policies were -- a stated scope reduction, not an assumed ENFORCED.

## Coverage statement

All 46 policies appear in `policy_enforcement_raw.json` with a `file:line` point or a `searched_for`
string. Complexity/API-surface/LHS outputs flag their reduced sample (20/335 files), not system-wide
coverage. No policy was dropped; no enforcement point was fabricated.
